chapter.title: Vehicles Other Than Railway or Tramway Rolling Stock, and Parts and Accessories Thereof

page.h1: HTS Chapter 87: Vehicles Other Than Railway or Tramway Rolling Stock, and Parts and Accessories Thereof — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Vehicles & Auto Parts by Market (HTS Ch. 87) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, Mexico, the EU, China, Korea and the Gulf charge on U.S. cars, trucks and auto parts, by market and product, with each market's vehicle-approval rules.

intro: Five of the nine largest markets charge nothing on U.S. vehicles: Mexico and South Korea under free-trade agreements, Australia under its FTA, Georgia on its own schedule, and the EU since July 1, 2026. Canada charges nothing on the vehicle itself but surtaxes its non-U.S. content, and China charges 25–35% on cars. For vehicles, though, the tariff is only half the story: every market has its own safety and emissions approval, and a U.S.-specification vehicle usually needs changes before it can be registered abroad — see each market's regulator below.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.name: Canada
markets.rule: CUSMA preferential tariff: 0% for U.S.-origin goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin. profile.headline: Canada is the largest market ($46.32B, down 13.7%). The vehicle itself enters free under CUSMA, but since April 9, 2025 Canada has charged a 25% surtax on the non-U.S. content of U.S.-built passenger vehicles and light trucks (the full value if the vehicle is not CUSMA-compliant). Parts (8708) are not on that list, so the $13.85B of parts crosses without the surtax.
profile.mainProducts: Auto parts: bumpers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, radiators, steering, airbags (8708) · Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs, hybrids, ATVs, golf carts and snowmobiles (8703)
profile.tariffNow: Free (CUSMA); 25% surtax on non-U.S. vehicle content

regulator.name: Transport Canada (Motor Vehicle Safety Act)
regulator.requirement: New vehicles sold in Canada must meet the Canadian Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (CMVSS) under the manufacturer's self-certification; meeting U.S. FMVSS alone is not enough

profile.headline: Mexico is the second-largest market ($26.05B, down 9.9%), and 72% of it is parts (8708, $18.88B) feeding Mexican assembly plants. Mexico's own MFN rate on cars is high (a WITS average of 35%), so a vehicle that fails USMCA's rules of origin loses most of its price advantage.
profile.mainProducts: Auto parts: bumpers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, radiators, steering, airbags (8708) · Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs, hybrids, ATVs, golf carts and snowmobiles (8703)

regulator.name: Secretaría de Economía (Mexican Official Standards, NOM)
regulator.requirement: Vehicles and parts sold in Mexico must meet the applicable Mexican Official Standards (NOMs) for safety and emissions; check the NOM for the specific product with the importer of record

profile.headline: The EU is the third-largest market ($17.30B, up 0.9%) and 71% of it is passenger vehicles (8703, $12.32B). Until July 1, 2026 the EU charged 10% on cars and about 13–16% on buses and heavy trucks; Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 cut all of it to zero, and the Commission can suspend that if the U.S. departs from the framework. Germany alone takes $9.06B.
profile.mainProducts: Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs, hybrids, ATVs, golf carts and snowmobiles (8703) · Auto parts: bumpers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, radiators, steering, airbags (8708)

regulator.name: EU type-approval authorities (Regulation (EU) 2018/858)
regulator.requirement: A new vehicle needs an EU type-approval and a certificate of conformity from a national approval authority before it can be sold or registered; U.S.-specification vehicles generally need modification first

profile.headline: Australia ($4.14B, down 18%) takes mostly pickups and trucks (8704, $1.32B), SUVs (8703, $1.02B) and parts. U.S. vehicles are tariff-free, but each model needs an Australian import approval and a place on the Register of Approved Vehicles, and Australia drives on the left, so right-hand-drive conversion is part of the cost.
profile.mainProducts: Trucks and pickups: light trucks, heavy trucks, dump trucks (8704) · Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs, hybrids, ATVs, golf carts and snowmobiles (8703)

regulator.name: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development (Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018)
regulator.requirement: Importing a road vehicle without approval is an offence; vehicles need an import approval and entry on the Register of Approved Vehicles (type approval or a concessional entry)

assumptions: MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 8703.23 for passenger cars and 8708.99 for parts) — using the most recent year WITS holds (2022 or 2023). National 8–10-digit lines can differ, and some use specific or compound duties.

USMCA (Mexico, Canada), KORUS (South Korea) and the Australia FTA apply 0% to qualifying U.S.-origin goods. For USMCA, vehicles and core parts must also meet the automotive rules of origin, otherwise the market's ordinary MFN rate applies; the normal-rate column shows that MFN rate.
For the EU, Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out chapter 87 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before that date.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to China's MFN rate, and a further 10% on the Annex 2 lines of Announcement 2025 No. 1 (tractors, cars with larger engines, pickups and trucks, agricultural trailers). China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods, valid unless a line is covered by an exclusion until December 31, 2026, are not added because exclusions are granted line by line.

Canada's cells show the CUSMA rate and the surtax lines named in the Canada Gazette: Motor Vehicles surtax SOR/2025-118 (8703 and 8704 passenger vehicles and light trucks) and the September 8, 2026 order SOR/2026-186 (8711.50 motorcycles, 8716.39 trailers). Neither order has a CUSMA exemption, though remission orders exist for some uses.
UAE, Saudi Arabia and Georgia show customs duty only. VAT, excise and registration fees are the buyer's business and are not included.
